docs.text: BMO: The Line-Following Arduino Robot # In fall 2025, I recreated the loveable gaming handheld character, BMO, from Adventure Time! This project lasted from late August to late November and was accomplished by an interdisciplinary team of two computer science majors, one computer engineer, one mechanical engineer, and one chemical engineer. As the project lead, my main priority was ensuring the team prototyped and developed the robot smoothly, taking in everyones' thoughts and opinions and communicating with teaching assistants and the professor for instruction and feedback. BB Era (Before BMO) # Before the robot was realized into BMO, my team and I protyped our own robots made from cardstock (an "origami bot"). These robots were simple in design, had an open top, and were programmed to simply go forward, turn on each side, then go backwards. There were a number of issues, such as batteries weighing down the chassis too much, lack of chassis integrity, and inconsistent wire connections. Sometimes, the bot would even work. However, despite these issues, it formed the base for the team's understanding of how to put together compontents together to form a working robot. AB Era (After BMO) # The next step for the team was to narrow down designs. It came down to two: BMO from Adventure Time, and the Krabby Patty Car from Spongebob. Since the project case was to design a robot for K-12 educational purposes, both designs came from cartoon shows to be as recognizeable as possible. Though we considered both strongly, we found that BMO would provide us with greater flexibility in technical features, but also a simplified design to avoid overengineering the chassis.
